hook.line: Looking for a place, a table or a cup of coffee, you will often want to say it doesn't matter which, or that you mean every single one. Spanish has small words for both.
hook.en:
Which day works for you?
Any day.

examples.es: Trabajo toda la mañana en el café.
examples.en: I work in the café all morning.

rule:
*Cada* means 'each' or 'every'. It never changes and never takes an article: *cada mesa*, *cada día*.

*Cualquier* means 'any at all' and goes before a noun: *cualquier día*, *cualquier persona*.
On its own it keeps the -a: *cualquiera*.

*Todo* is about the whole thing, and it matches the noun:
*toda la mañana* (all morning)
*todo el barrio* (the whole neighbourhood)
*todos los días* (every day)

So 'every day' can be *cada día* or *todos los días*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *cada*, *cualquier* and *todo* quantifiers; *cualquiera* is an indefinite pronoun.

options: Any of them will do for me.

readAndPick.es: Trabajo toda la mañana en el café.
options: I work in the café every morning.
I work in the café all morning.
Each of them can come in.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ mesa tiene su historia.* (*Cada* or *Cualquiera*)
yourTurn.why: You mean each table in turn, so *cada*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type: *Puedes venir ___ día.* (*cualquier* or *cualquiera*)
yourTurn.why: Before a noun it shortens to *cualquier*.
With no noun after it, it keeps the -a.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Each customer orders something different.
yourTurn.why: *Cada* stays singular and has no article.
Alone it is *cualquiera*; with *persona* it is *cualquier*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I work all morning in the café.
yourTurn.answer: Trabajo toda la mañana en el café.
accept: Toda la mañana trabajo en el café.
yourTurn.why: 'All morning' is the whole of it, so *toda la mañana*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it with *cada*: *Todos los días como aquí.*
yourTurn.why: *Cada* is singular, so *cada día*, not *cada días*.

pitfalls.why: *Cada* always points at one at a time, so the noun stays singular.
Almost. Before a noun, *cualquiera* loses its -a.
Nothing follows it, so it keeps the -a: *cualquiera*.
*Cada* never takes an article. Use *todos los días* if you want one.

personal: Say something true about your week using *cada*, and something you don't mind about using *cualquier* or *cualquiera*.
